mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as low interest rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, prompting risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 8.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based consumer demand slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: During supply shock regimes (INDPRO decline > 5.0% monthly), S&P 500 forward returns are negative due to reduced corporate earnings and heightened economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of supply shock regimes (INDPRO decline > 5.0% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS > 100k) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as it signals robust labor market conditions and consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 45% of months when PAYEMS > 100k (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 2.0% signals a monetary tightening cycle, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) indicate stagflation risk, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to eroding real returns and policy uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% over 3 months), S&P 500 forward returns are negative due to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% over 3 months).
